key_insight: Silicon oxynitride-doped silicon enables laser-inscribed flexible Bragg gratings with UV-to-NIR reflection for authentication applications.
engineering_relevance: Fabrication below 100 °C and refractive-index control from 2.1 to 2.5 offer a route to flexible photonic structures that preserve laser-written micro-information.
method: Synthesize silicon oxynitride-doped silicon on flexible substrates and inscribe Bragg gratings using ultrafast lasers.
Probe local structure with soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Si L, O K and N K edges.
Investigate formation mechanisms with quantum calculations and predict bulk Si3N4−xOx structures using particle swarm optimization coupled with DFT.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical and experimental demonstrations of micro-information preservation through multispectral reflection, but provides no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Durability under repeated bending and authentication reliability remain unquantified in the abstract.
paper_title: Design and synthesis of laser inscribed flexible Bragg gratings containing silicon oxynitride-doped silicon thin film for authentication applications with the insights from X-Ray Absorption Spectroscopy and Quantum Mechanical Calculations
